notes: Offline, no repository and no pull request: the three prompts exercise the setup path only. The harness controls the environment of each run — `all-ok` runs with the normal PATH and a working gh login; `jq-missing` runs with a PATH from which every directory holding `jq` is replaced by a shim directory that mirrors it without `jq` (dropping the directory outright also drops gh, sed or tr); `gh-unauth` runs with GH_TOKEN empty and GH_CONFIG_DIR pointing at an empty temporary directory. The answer file is the agent's final reply, verbatim. The install hint the grader expects follows the OS of the run (`--os`).

evals.name: all-ok
evals.prompt: check that my machine has everything pr-guardian needs
evals.expected_output: The doctor's ok lines relayed verbatim, one line saying the machine is ready, nothing invented.
assertions: the doctor lines appear in order: ok bash, git, gh, gh auth, jq, timeout, state
the answer says the machine is ready or there is nothing to fix
no invented install command (no brew, winget, apt or dnf install)

evals.name: jq-missing
evals.prompt: set up pr-guardian on this machine
evals.expected_output: The doctor's lines with `FAIL  jq:` verbatim, the script's own install command proposed as a question, nothing run.
assertions: a `FAIL  jq:` line is present verbatim
the proposed command is the hint the script printed for this OS
it does not claim to have installed anything
the other checks are still listed (ok    gh auth)

evals.name: gh-unauth
evals.prompt: is my setup ready for pr-guardian?
evals.expected_output: The doctor's lines with `FAIL  gh auth:` verbatim, the user told to run `gh auth login` themselves, the scopes check reported as skipped.
assertions: a `FAIL  gh auth:` line is present
the answer tells the user to run gh auth login themselves
it does not claim to be authenticated now
the scopes check is reported as skipped or not run, never invented
